note: Year ranges are HumAIn Logic editorial estimates, NOT figures published by the cited sources. None of the cited sources gives per-occupation 'full automation' dates. Method: (1) relative automation susceptibility per occupation from Frey & Osborne (2013) probabilities and task-exposure scores in Eloundou et al. (2023) and ILO (2023); (2) anchored to McKinsey (2023) 'Economic potential of generative AI', which estimates half of today's work activities could be automated between 2030 and 2060 (midpoint ~2045); (3) adjusted for physical/manual tasks (slower robotics adoption), regulation/licensing, and BLS/WEF employment outlooks. 'Near-full automation' means most of the occupation's current tasks can be done by technology at scale; it does not imply all jobs disappear, and several sources (OECD, IMF, WEF) stress augmentation and job transformation over replacement. Confidence reflects agreement among sources and technical maturity, and is low for most ranges. Source URLs were checked on 2026-10-14; IMF, WEF, OECD and BLS pages block automated fetches (HTTP 403) but are the official landing pages confirmed via web search.
